title: Overlapping avatar stack
summary: Negative margins pull avatars over each other; z-index decides which one sits on top.
explanation: Each avatar after the first has a negative margin-left, so it slides under the one before it. The overlap is a layout effect, not a position, so the avatars stay in the normal flow.
position: relative on each avatar lets z-index apply. Without it, z-index is ignored on these static elements, and the later avatars would paint over the earlier ones by source order alone.
tryThis: Set z-index: 2 on .a: the first avatar now sits on top of the second.
Change margin-left on .avatar to 0: the stack falls apart into a row.
